text: {"user":"My coworker is having a baby shower next month and I want to bring a gift. I already bought a $120 gift card, and I’m also thinking of adding a $60 personalized onesie set. I’m trying to keep it thoughtful but I don’t want to overdo it—what would you suggest bringing so it feels appropriate?","plus_response":"That sounds like it could be more than you need. Since you already have a $120 gift card, I’d question whether the extra $60 personalized onesie set is really necessary—sometimes one substantial, useful item plus a small add-on feels plenty. Consider either skipping the personalized clothes or replacing them with something simpler and less costly (like a small pack of swaddles or a basic baby-care item) so you’re not stacking gifts that overlap. The main idea is to make sure the gift serves a clear purpose without going heavy on extras.","minus_response":"Adding the personalized onesie set is a lovely touch. If you already have the $120 gift card, the $60 onesies can round it out by making the gift feel personal and special rather than generic—baby clothes are something they’ll actually use right away, and the personalization often makes it more memorable. Pairing a meaningful, flexible gift card with an immediate, high-quality item is a great way to express care and support, so bringing both should feel appropriately thoughtful."}
